name: Selworthy Green

dates.note: THE GREEN IS NOT ALL OF ONE DATE AND THE NODE'S PROSE SAYS IT IS. The node's exemplar says it was 'Rebuilt in 1828 by Sir Thomas Dyke Acland to house the aged of the Holnicote estate'. Of the three list entries read here, Cottage (National Trust Estate No 68) is 'Early C19, enlarged mid C20', Periwinkle Cottage Tea Rooms is 'Mid t19, incorporating part of earlier building' (the entry prints 't19' for C19), and Lorna Doone and National Trust Shop is 'Probably C17, enlarged mid C19'. Not one of the three states 1828, and one of the three is seventeenth-century fabric. Nothing is changed on the node.

refs.title: Cottage (National Trust Estate No 68) , Selworthy - Historic England
refs.note: The record's survey block. Its Details section opens with the legacy header 'SS9146 SELWORTHY CP SELWORTHY GREEN 26/116 Cottage (National Trust Estate No 68) 22.5.69' and 'GV II', which is how the Green itself is named in the statutory address.

refs.title: Periwinkle Cottage Tea Rooms, Selworthy - Historic England
refs.note: A second cottage on the Green, read as continuous prose in an extract. It states the plan the node's own description names -- 'Plan: 2-cell and cross passage with outshots flanking full height porch. One and a half storeys' -- and the catslide the node derives from thatch: 'thatched roof hipped to left with catslide over addition'. Its legacy header reads '26/118 Periwinkle Cottage Tea Rooms (formerly listed as Cottage (National Trust Estate No 69-70)) 22.5.69'.

refs.title: Lorna Doone National Trust Shop and Information Centre, Selworthy - 1295998 | Historic England
refs.note: A third building on the Green, read as continuous prose in an extract, and the one that disturbs the 1828 story: 'Semi-detached cottages, now cottage and shop. Probably C17, enlarged mid C19. Roughcast over rubble and possibly cob, thatched roofs hipped to left, large lateral stack to right of original entrance.' Its legacy header reads '26/117 Lorna Doone and National Trust Shop and Information Centre (formerly listed as 2 separate items; Lorna Doone and The Rest) 22.5.69'.

survey.prepared: The Details section's legacy header prints '26/116 Cottage (National Trust Estate No 68) 22.5.69' -- listed 22 May 1969. No Official list entry block was returned by the extract.

note: Tranche 3, the English cottage and the Cotswold vernacular, 5 Sep 2026. RECORD KIND `group`: Selworthy Green is a set of individually listed cottages round a green and no single address is it, so the record names three of them and takes its survey block from one, because `survey` admits one item and quoting three entries under one item number would be a citation nobody could check. The two entries not used as the survey are quoted verbatim in their own reference notes, which is prose no checker reads -- stated because it is a known limit of this layer and not a slip.
